critical_code_review_comments: server.py file has grown to ~1220 lines with WebSocket + file validation additions. Recommend modularization for maintainability.

WebSocket handler uses `asyncio.create_task(persist_changes())` for each incoming message. Under rapid typing this creates many concurrent tasks that all take `save_lock`. The `latest_content` 'debounce' pattern works (tasks that lose the race become no-ops), but a single background writer task with an asyncio.Event would be cleaner and generate less DB traffic.

WebSocket auth uses 4401 close code on rejection which is a valid application-defined code, but browsers surface `wasClean=false` regardless; consider also sending a close reason string for easier debugging.

File validation reads entire file into memory (contents = await file.read()) before checking size — a client could theoretically stream up to available RAM before hitting the 10MB check. For production, prefer content-length header pre-check or streaming with early-abort. Acceptable for 10MB limit / MVP.

useDocumentSocket.js only reconnects on documentId change — if the WS drops mid-session (network blip) it does not auto-reconnect, and user only sees 'Offline' with no retry. Consider exponential-backoff reconnect.
